points.description: Shows that theta_ss = theta_d is impossible, by substitution or torque-balance argument (at rest with theta = theta_d = 90 deg the PD torque is zero but gravity torque mgl sin90 = 2.4525 N·m is non-zero; the proportional term must supply holding torque, so an error is needed).

levels.says: Only the qualitative statement that PD (no integral action) gives steady-state error, without the gravity/torque-balance or substitution argument.

points.description: Correct steady-state equation obtained by setting theta-dot = theta-ddot = 0: Kp(theta_d - theta_ss) = m g l sin(theta_ss) (Kd term vanishes).

Correct steady-state error value: about 0.049 rad = 2.81 deg (accept 2.7 to 2.9 deg or 0.047 to 0.050 rad, by linearised estimate e = mgl/Kp, iteration, or graphical solution; theta_ss about 87.2 deg). Using sin(theta_ss) ~ theta_ss (small-angle about zero) is wrong and earns nothing here. Answer in radians with no conversion to degrees loses the unit share.

levels.says: Correct method (linearisation or numerical solution of the equation) but arithmetic slip, or value only given as theta_ss without stating the error; or value from a wrong operating point (e.g. cos 60 deg in denominator) that lands in range by coincidence.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the impossibility argument, the equation Kp(θd−θss)=mgℓ sinθss, and an error of about 2.81° (2.7–2.9°). Qualitative "no integral action" alone earns half of P1. Small-angle sinθ≈θ loses the value marks; a numerical solution giving only θss without the error earns 3 of 4 in total.
rubric.answer_key: Plant with PD: J θ̈ + bθ̇ + mgℓ sinθ = Kp(θd − θ) − Kd θ̇. Steady state (θ̇=θ̈=0): Kp(θd − θss) = mgℓ sinθss. mgℓ = 1×9.81×0.25 = 2.4525 N·m. If θss = θd = 90°, LHS = 0 but RHS = 2.4525 ≠ 0, so the joint cannot rest at θd. With e = θd − θss, sinθss ≈ sinθd − e cosθd = 1 (cos90° = 0), so e ≈ 2.4525/50 = 0.04905 rad = 2.81°. Numerical solution gives θss ≈ 87.19°, e ≈ 2.81°. Final: steady-state error ≈ 2.81 degrees (θss ≈ 87.2°).
